name: page-header
title: Page header
description: Page header. Best for: The top of every screen: its one h1, with eyebrow, description, breadcrumbs and page actions.

files.content:
import type { ReactNode, Ref } from 'react' import { cn } from '../../../lib/cn' export type PageHeaderProps = { /** The page's name: the h1's text, and so the name of any region that points at `id`. */ title: string /** A short mono label above the title: the section the page belongs to ("Operations"). */ eyebrow?: ReactNode /** One or two sentences under the title. */ description?: ReactNode /** The page's own actions, usually one or two Buttons. They sit at the trailing edge and drop * under the title when the row runs out of room. */ actions?: ReactNode /** A `Breadcrumbs` trail, drawn above everything else. */ breadcrumbs?: ReactNode /** Lands on the h1, not the wrapper, so `
` is named by the title. */ id?: string /** 1, the page's title, unless the header sits inside a page that already has its h1: a pane, * a tab panel, a docs example. Then 2. */ level?: 1 | 2 className?: string ref?: Ref } /** * The top of a screen: an optional breadcrumb trail, an optional eyebrow, the page's one h1, an * optional description, and the page's own actions at the trailing edge. * * The h1 is the AGENTS.md page title exactly, `font-display font-semibold text-2xl`, stepping to * `text-3xl` once the header is given 48rem: a screen that wrote its own h1 before this existed * and one that uses this component read as the same page. A page has one h1 and this is it; a * heading further down the page is a SectionHeading. `level={2}` exists for the one case where a * page-shaped header sits inside another page (a pane, a tab panel, a docs example): the docs page * for this component drew four h1s before it existed. The look does not change with the level. * * The eyebrow is the system's label role (mono, 12px, uppercase, tracked) in `text.muted`, and a * `p` above the h1 rather than a span inside it, so the page is announced as "Inventory" and not * as "Operations Inventory". Reading order is still eyebrow then title, as it is drawn. * * The breadcrumbs slot comes first in the DOM, so "where am I" is heard before "what is this", * the order every screen reader user meets on a site that has a trail at all. It is a slot, not * an `items` array, so the trail keeps its own `renderLink` and `maxItems` and this component * never has to re-export them. * * `@container` on the root, the way SectionHeading does it: the title steps up and the actions * wrap with the width the header is given, not with the viewport, so the same header works in a * full page and in a narrow pane beside a sidebar. * * A `div`, not a `header`. Inside `main` a `header` is a plain group, and outside it, which is * where a header near the top of a layout often ends up, it becomes a second banner landmark * beside the shell's own. * * Contrast rows, by exact name: title "text.primary on surface.base"; eyebrow "text.muted on * surface.base"; description "text.secondary on surface.base". */ export function PageHeader({ title, eyebrow, description, actions, breadcrumbs, id, level = 1, className, ref, }: PageHeaderProps) { const Heading = level === 2 ? 'h2' : 'h1' return (
